stem: A client at high risk for pressure injury is being repositioned regularly but has early sacral skin changes. Which additional intervention is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue the standard mattress and rely on repositioning alone because support-surface selection does not affect pressure-injury prevention.
options.B: Reduce skin assessment frequency because repeated inspection increases friction and can worsen early sacral changes.
options.C: Stop routine repositioning after adding a cushion because a pressure-relieving device replaces the need for position changes.
options.D: Use an appropriate pressure-redistributing support surface while continuing individualized repositioning and regular skin assessment.

rationale: Pressure-injury prevention requires a combined approach. Current VA guidance recommends regular skin inspection, regular repositioning, and support surfaces such as special mattresses, overlays, or cushions that reduce pressure. Therefore D is best: an appropriate pressure-redistributing support surface is added while repositioning and skin surveillance continue. A incorrectly assumes a standard mattress is necessarily adequate. B incorrectly reduces surveillance despite evolving skin findings. C incorrectly treats a support surface as a substitute for repositioning.
educational_objective: Select a pressure-redistributing support surface as an adjunct—not a replacement—for repositioning and skin assessment in a client at high risk for pressure injury.
source_document_title: Take Steps to Prevent Pressure Injuries
source_version_date: Current Veterans Health Library guidance; annual review 2025-12-01

source_claim_supported: VA guidance supports regular skin inspection, regular repositioning, and pressure-reducing support surfaces as complementary prevention measures.

source_original.stem: A client at high risk for pressure injury is being repositioned regularly but has early sacral skin changes. Which additional intervention is most appropriate?

options.A: Continue the standard mattress and rely on repositioning alone because support-surface selection does not affect pressure-injury prevention.
options.B: Reduce skin assessment frequency because repeated inspection increases friction and can worsen early sacral changes.
options.C: Stop routine repositioning after adding a cushion because a pressure-relieving device replaces the need for position changes.
options.D: Use an appropriate pressure-redistributing support surface while continuing individualized repositioning and regular skin assessment.

source_original.rationale: A high-risk client with early sacral skin changes needs a combined prevention approach. VA guidance supports regular skin inspection, repositioning, and appropriate support surfaces that reduce pressure. A support surface does not replace repositioning or surveillance, and a standard mattress should not be assumed adequate when skin changes are already emerging.
source_original.source_detail: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Take Steps to Prevent Pressure Injuries: inspect skin regularly, reposition according to risk/condition, and use appropriate pressure-reducing/support surfaces such as special mattresses, overlays, or cushions when indicated. Current VA Veterans Health Library pressure-injury prevention guidance; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: mobility, positioning, skin integrity, elimination and nonpharmacologic comfort activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the stem, answer key, and core construct. Updated the source URL to the current VA Veterans Health Library article and tightened the rationale to the directly supported combined prevention measures without claiming a universal support-surface type or turning interval.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Library guidance.
audit_findings.currentness: VA article carries annual review date 2025-12-01 and was rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: The prevention section explicitly lists skin inspection, repositioning, and support surfaces.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No unsupported support-surface specification, mandatory interval, or staging diagnosis was added.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because support surfaces are a recognized pressure-reduction intervention and repositioning alone is not the only prevention strategy.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because current skin changes strengthen, not weaken, the need for surveillance.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because adding a support surface does not justify stopping repositioning.
distractor_audit.D: Directly matches the multimodal prevention approach supported by VA guidance.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D combines all appropriate measures without discarding a necessary prevention component.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address pressure-injury prevention strategy and are similar in scope.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Basic Care and Comfort through positioning, skin integrity, and nonpharmacologic preventive care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review checked whether support-surface use was overstated as replacing repositioning or whether a specific product/frequency was implied; final wording avoids both.
